1.why: The system enforces server-side authorization by deriving owner identity only from authenticated session (see authenticated() and MFA routes).

2.why: The same verification code (TEST_IDENTITY_CODE) works for any user, as it is hardcoded and not user-specific.

3.why: Previous sessions remain valid after MFA is enabled (no explicit invalidation of old sessions on MFA enablement).

4.why: OTP shared secret and backup codes are stored encrypted (AES-GCM) or hashed (SHA-256 with salt) at rest.

5.why: Secrets and codes are generated using crypto.getRandomValues(), a cryptographically secure RNG.

6.why: Secrets, OTPs, and session tokens are kept out of browser storage and non-HttpOnly cookies (stored in memory or HttpOnly/Secure cookies).

7.why: Server-side input validation is performed (e.g., isEmail, isPhone, isOtp, hasForeignIdentity checks).

8.why: Contextual output encoding is used (e.g., escText function in HTML, JSON responses).

9.why: Redirects are restricted to an allow-list (allowedRedirect function checks for '/' or '/mfa').

10.why: Secure response headers are set (CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, etc.).

11.why: Session cookies are set with HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict attributes.

12.why: OTP seeds, backup codes, and session tokens are kept out of logs, URLs, and error output (no exposure in code).

13.why: Verification codes are single-use (e.g., check.used, enrollment.used flags) and time-bound (expires checks).

14.why: Repeated failed verification attempts are rate-limited (failed() function locks after 5 failures).

15.why: Session identifier is rotated on authentication (rotateAuthenticated), has idle/absolute timeouts, and is invalidated on logout.
